\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تعداد} (tādād)}{تعداد (tādād)}]{\ur{تعداد} (tādād) — a number (of people or things); a count}

\label{lesson:UR-C376-tadad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for tremendous, then the Urdu for severe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تعداد}}
\textbf{\ur{تعداد}} — \emph{tādād} — \textquotedblleft{}a number (of people or things); a count\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تعداد} \ur{زیادہ} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{کمرہ} \ur{چھوٹا} \ur{پڑے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tādād zyādā huī to kamrā chhoṭā paṛe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there are too many people, the room will be too small.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تعداد}} (\emph{tādād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taʿdād}, \textquotedblleft{}counting\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tādād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tādād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tādād zyādā huī to kamrā chhoṭā paṛe gā.} — If there are too many people, the room will be too small.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for tremendous, then the Urdu for severe, then say \emph{tādād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تعداد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A number (of people or things); a count\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مقدار} (miqdār)}{مقدار (miqdār)}]{\ur{مقدار} (miqdār) — an amount; a quantity}

\label{lesson:UR-C376-miqdar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for severe, then the Urdu for a count.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مقدار}}
\textbf{\ur{مقدار}} — \emph{miqdār} — \textquotedblleft{}an amount; a quantity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{دوا} \ur{کی} \ur{مقدار} \ur{زیادہ} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{نقصان} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar davā kī miqdār zyādā huī to nuqsān ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the dose is too large, it will do harm.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مقدار}} (\emph{miqdār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{miqdār}, \textquotedblleft{}a measure, an amount\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miqdār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar davā kī miqdār zyādā huī to nuqsān ho gā.} — If the dose is too large, it will do harm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for severe, then the Urdu for a count, then say \emph{miqdār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معمولی} (māmūlī)}{معمولی (māmūlī)}]{\ur{معمولی} (māmūlī) — minor; ordinary}

\label{lesson:UR-C376-mamuli}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a count, then the Urdu for an amount.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معمولی}}
\textbf{\ur{معمولی}} — \emph{māmūlī} — \textquotedblleft{}minor; ordinary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{چوٹ} \ur{معمولی} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہسپتال} \ur{جانے} \ur{کی} \ur{ضرورت} \ur{نہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar choṭ māmūlī hai to haspatāl jāne kī zarūrat nahīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the injury is minor, there is no need to go to hospital.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معمولی}} (\emph{māmūlī}) is built on \emph{māmūl}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{maʿmūl}, \textquotedblleft{}customary, done as usual\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māmūlī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar choṭ māmūlī hai to haspatāl jāne kī zarūrat nahīṅ.} — If the injury is minor, there is no need to go to hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a count, then the Urdu for an amount, then say \emph{māmūlī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ} (lag-bhag)}{لگ بھگ (lag-bhag)}]{\ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ} (lag-bhag) — about; approximately}

\label{lesson:UR-C376-lag-bhag}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an amount, then the Urdu for minor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ}}
\textbf{\ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ}} — \emph{lag-bhag} — \textquotedblleft{}about; approximately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ابھی} \ur{چلے} \ur{تو} \ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ} \ur{دو} \ur{گھنٹے} \ur{لگیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar abhī chale to lag-bhag do ghanṭe lageṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we leave now, it will take about two hours.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ}} (\emph{lag-bhag}) is built on \emph{lag}, \textquotedblleft{}near, up to\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lag} under Sanskrit \emph{lagna}, \textquotedblleft{}attached\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10893); \emph{bhag} is a rhyming partner with no meaning of its own, as far as our sources show.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lag-bhag}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar abhī chale to lag-bhag do ghanṭe lageṅ ge.} — If we leave now, it will take about two hours.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an amount, then the Urdu for minor, then say \emph{lag-bhag} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حد} (had)}{حد (had)}]{\ur{حد} (had) — a limit}

\label{lesson:UR-C376-had}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for minor, then the Urdu for approximately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حد}}
\textbf{\ur{حد}} — \emph{had} — \textquotedblleft{}a limit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{نے} \ur{حد} \ur{پار} \ur{کی} \ur{تو} \ur{جرمانہ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp ne had pār kī to jurmānā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you go past the limit, there will be a fine.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حد}} (\emph{had}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥadd}, \textquotedblleft{}a boundary, a limit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}
